title: South Korea Air Force Officer 2026: Routes, Tests and Training
metaDescription: Complete 2026 guide to ROK Air Force officer routes: Academy admission, candidate courses, age and education rules, fitness tests, interviews and training.
headline: Become a South Korea Air Force Officer: 2026 Complete Guide

sections.title: Officer Routes into the ROK Air Force
sections.content:
The Republic of Korea Air Force commissions officers mainly through the Korea Air Force Academy, a four-year degree programme that combines academic study, military training and flight-related education. Graduates are commissioned as second lieutenants and begin service in flying, engineering, air defence or support branches.

Other routes include officer candidate courses for university graduates and specialist branches such as medicine, law and engineering. Each route has its own age limits and academic requirements, published in the annual recruitment notice, so candidates should confirm the route that matches their education and career goals.

sections.title: Eligibility: Age, Education and Citizenship
sections.content:
Air Force Academy cadets are typically school leavers admitted through a competitive national selection process that weighs academic results, fitness and interviews. Officer candidate routes generally require a bachelor's degree, with age limits that vary by route and branch, so the official notice for the relevant year is the authoritative source.

All officer candidates must be South Korean citizens with a clean record and the medical fitness required for military service. Dual citizenship and certain medical conditions can affect eligibility, and candidates should check these points early rather than after passing written tests.

sections.title: Selection Tests and Fitness Standards
sections.content:
Selection typically includes a written examination covering academic subjects and aptitude, a physical fitness assessment, a medical examination, a personality assessment and panel interviews. Fitness tests commonly cover running, push-ups and sit-ups, with standards adjusted by age and gender.

Pilot candidates face additional stages, including aptitude testing for flying and stricter vision and medical standards. Preparation should therefore combine academic revision, regular fitness training and practice for interviews, since each stage can eliminate candidates independently.

sections.title: Training and Career Progression
sections.content:
Academy cadets spend four years studying engineering, humanities or sciences alongside military drill, leadership training and physical conditioning, before commissioning. Officer candidates complete a shorter intensive course covering military skills, leadership and branch-specific training.

After commissioning, officers serve in operational units, attend career courses and may specialise further in flying, maintenance, air traffic control or logistics. Promotion depends on performance, qualifications and time in rank, and long-serving officers can reach senior command positions.

faqs.q: How do you become an officer in the South Korea Air Force?
faqs.a: The main route is the Korea Air Force Academy, a four-year degree programme combining academic study, military training and flight-related education, after which graduates are commissioned as second lieutenants. University graduates can also apply through officer candidate courses and specialist branches such as medicine, law and engineering, depending on their qualifications.

faqs.q: What are the age and education requirements for ROKAF officers?
faqs.a: Air Force Academy cadets are typically school leavers admitted through competitive national selection, while officer candidate routes generally require a bachelor's degree with age limits that vary by route and branch. Candidates should always check the official annual recruitment notice, since limits and eligible degrees change between intakes.

faqs.q: What tests are included in ROKAF officer selection?
faqs.a: Selection typically includes a written examination covering academic subjects and aptitude, a physical fitness assessment, a medical examination, a personality assessment and panel interviews. Pilot candidates face additional flying aptitude tests and stricter vision and medical standards, so preparation should cover academics, fitness and interview practice together.

faqs.q: Where does ROKAF officer training take place?
faqs.a: Academy cadets train at the Korea Air Force Academy over four years, studying academic subjects alongside military drill, leadership training and physical conditioning. Officer candidates complete a shorter intensive course at designated training centres, including facilities around Jinju, before joining their operational units.
